Exploratory Data Analysis

Only using selected classes as all other classes in data set are commmon among all students within data set

Stats comfort

Shows high correlation towards pstat 100, 115, and 131, and 134. Bit weird because those are the more coding heavy classes and not stats heavy classes. Negative correlation for pstat 160, 174, and 175 is also interesting bc they are the more advanced theoretical stats classes. Boxplots shows this same trend but also highlights heavy variation and overlap from groups. Cs classes also show negative correlation.

##   stat.comf   PSTAT_100   PSTAT_115   PSTAT_131   PSTAT_134   PSTAT_160 
##  1.00000000  0.06639935  0.08624924  0.06591115  0.07966783 -0.10097405 
##   PSTAT_174   PSTAT_175       CS_16 
## -0.17822376 -0.16164260 -0.17427633

Stats proficiency

Shows high correlation towards pstat 100, 115, and 131. Bit weird because those are the more coding heavy classes and not stats heavy classes. Negative correlation for pstat 134. Negative correlation for 160, 174, and 175 is also interesting bc they are the more advanced theoretical stats classes. Boxplots shows this same trend but also highlights heavy variation and overlap from groups.

##   stat.prof   PSTAT_100   PSTAT_115   PSTAT_131   PSTAT_134   PSTAT_160 
##  1.00000000  0.07275726  0.17534472  0.30842368 -0.03876704 -0.08703883 
##   PSTAT_174   PSTAT_175       CS_16 
## -0.17069719 -0.11236664 -0.31101230

Math comfort

Math comfort is fairly random among classes.

##   math.comf   PSTAT_100   PSTAT_115   PSTAT_131   PSTAT_134   PSTAT_160 
##  1.00000000 -0.01594032 -0.10372348  0.12892073  0.03943379 -0.19069252 
##   PSTAT_174   PSTAT_175       CS_16 
##  0.03739788  0.09437014  0.08999541

Math proficiency

Shows similar trend as stats where the stats classes that actualy utilize a lot of theoretical and advanced math show negative correlation with proficiency.

##   math.prof   PSTAT_100   PSTAT_115   PSTAT_131   PSTAT_134   PSTAT_160 
##  1.00000000  0.03767888 -0.10215671  0.14185987 -0.12368452 -0.16903085 
##   PSTAT_174   PSTAT_175       CS_16 
## -0.18232322 -0.18184824  0.04558423

Programming comfort

Programming comfort Shows high correlation towards pstat 100, 115, 131, and 134. Negative correlation for 160, 174, and 175. Interestingly enough no strong correlation for computer science classes.

##   prog.comf   PSTAT_100   PSTAT_115   PSTAT_131   PSTAT_134   PSTAT_160 
##  1.00000000  0.06501579  0.15668780  0.22276504  0.34995662 -0.11111111 
##   PSTAT_174   PSTAT_175       CS_16 
## -0.02905424 -0.01912584 -0.04869221

Programming proficiency

Programming comfort Shows high proficiency towards pstat 131 and 134. Pretty much no correlation for other stats classes. Interestingly enough there is a negative correlation for cs 16.

##    prog.prof    PSTAT_100    PSTAT_115    PSTAT_131    PSTAT_134    PSTAT_160 
##  1.000000000 -0.009752369  0.022160132  0.270426394  0.217927531  0.025000000 
##    PSTAT_174    PSTAT_175        CS_16 
## -0.004902903 -0.058094750 -0.155065968

Data analysis

Used linear regression as simple predictor for comfort and proficiency for stats, math, and programming. Unfortunately nothing is too significant as a predictor for comfort or profficiency, there are mor just general trends among the data. It is important to note data set is tiny so such trends kind of only can be observed as generalizations with very little reliable statistical backing. ### Statistics comfort

comf_stat <- lm(stat.comf ~ PSTAT_100+PSTAT_115+PSTAT_131+PSTAT_134+PSTAT_160+PSTAT_174+PSTAT_175+CS_16, data = mini)
summary(comf_stat)
